data.summary: The `yq` directory is a container-image provisioning scenario in an aio-config generation system. It pairs a `scenario.toml` metadata descriptor with a `fragment.Dockerfile` install recipe, together declaring how to install the yq YAML/JSON/XML command-line processor via the mise tool manager. There is no application business logic here — it is purely an infrastructure/configuration layer for reproducible tool installation.

file_insights.name: scenario.toml
file_insights.summary: Machine-readable metadata describing the yq install scenario (id, category, installer, and the pinned 4.53.6 version) that `aio-config gen` consumes during fragment resolution.
file_insights.source_summary: Defines scalar fields `id = "yq"`, `name`, `description` (YAML/JSON/XML CLI processor, mise aqua backend, installed under /opt/mise/installs), `category = "shell"`, `installer = "mise"`, plus a `[[versions]]` table with label and version both set to 4.53.6. Also contains comments explaining that the sibling fragment.Dockerfile holds the actual install steps.
file_insights.detailed_description: This TOML file is the declarative descriptor for the yq scenario, telling the aio-config generator that yq is a shell-category tool installed through mise. It carries the pinned version list (4.53.6) that the fragment template substitutes into install commands, keeping version management centralized and decoupled from the Dockerfile mechanics.
responsibilities: Declare the unique scenario identifier and human-readable name
Specify the install category (shell) and installer backend (mise)
Pin the yq version (4.53.6) used by fragment generation
Point consumers to the adjacent fragment.Dockerfile for install steps

file_insights.name: fragment.Dockerfile
file_insights.summary: Dockerfile fragment that installs yq at a parameterized version via `mise use -g` and then verifies the binary is resolvable in both login and non-login shells.
file_insights.source_summary: A single RUN instruction interpolates `ARG YQ_VERSION={{version}}` into `mise use -g "yq@${YQ_VERSION}"`, lists installed tools via `mise ls yq`, and runs two guard commands (`bash -lc` and `bash -c`) that verify `command -v yq` succeeds, emitting a MISSING error and non-zero exit otherwise.
file_insights.detailed_description: This Docker layer performs the actual provisioning of yq inside the image, using the `YQ_VERSION` ARG injected by the scenario generator. Because `mise use -g` is read-modify-write over the global mise config, the fragment is idempotent and safely composable with other mise-based fragments without a separate aggregation step. It concludes with login and non-login shell PATH sanity checks that fail the build if the `yq` binary cannot be located.
responsibilities: Install yq at the scenario-pinned version using mise
Remain idempotent and composable with other mise tool fragments
Verify the yq binary is on PATH in login and non-login shells
Fail the image build early if yq is not resolvable
